Painted night shipyard on the beach, close low angle right up against the curved side of the ship's hull, which fills most of the frame. The ship is hauled up on timber rollers (copy the attached ship board for the ship design only: ornate red-and-gold lacquered hull with painted panels, one great crimson battened sail furled above; repaint it at night by firelight). A fresh pale timber plank is fitted flush into a gap in the red hull's side. One shadowy blacksmith, a faceless dark silhouette with a bare, broad, sweat-glistening back, stands pressed hard against the hull and drives a long, thick iron spike straight into the plank and deep into the ship with a heavy hammer, stroke after stroke; a hot fan of sparks bursts at every thrust, the plank bowing into the hull, a row of spikes already driven home to the head along the seam. The forge fire roars behind him, steam bursts off a quench tub, the great red sail shudders above. Amber #e0a33c forge light, violet-rose #d98fa8 night sky. Hard rhythm, heat, sweat, pounding. PAINTED STILL — no faces and no recognisable person: the only figure is one anonymous dark silhouette, a shadow-shape against the light that belongs to the place; the place or object IS the subject. Openly erotic metaphor: the shapes, wetness, swelling, thrusting and release unmistakably read as bodies and sex, the way a frank erotic painting does — yet everything stays landscape and object, no nudity, no literal anatomy. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
